pr_title: Half close port forwarding connections to fix hangs
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->
Fixes: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6842

See the comment here for a full explanation of the bug: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6842#issuecomment-1397473939

The core change here is to close the write side of the `net.Conn` to the client in order to signal that client that the response is complete.

The base `net.Conn` however doesn't expose a function to close only the writer, so everything is changed to use `net.TCPListener` which does. The bulk of the change is to support that a little more cleanly.
pr_comments: 👋 @josebalius I know this isn't your space anymore, but you're probably the expert on this code still 😅 If you still have context, would appreciate confirmation on my understanding of how the flow works - thanks!

While you're working on this @cmbrose, note that port forwarding tests have been disabled in CI due to being flakey https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/71ec2c4e2305ba6ac17962f0805aee5fe8415584/pkg/liveshare/port_forwarder_test.go#L37 and that some other ports-related tests might be flakey as well https://github.com/cli/cli/discussions/6858#discussioncomment-4711405

> not sure why we need a half closer, can't we close both the read and write?

@josebalius we need to keep the read side open so that the local side can still write a reply after the codespace finishes the response. That flow would look like this:

1. local app sends a request to forwarded port
2. `gh` receives the request on the TCP connection `io.Reader` and forwards to the ssh channel `io.Writer`
3. ssh channel sends the request to the codespace, which responds and closes its own TCP write connection
4. ssh channel in `gh` receives the codespace response in its `io.Reader` and forwards the reply to the TCP connection
5. ssh channel's reader reads EOF and exits the `io.Copy` call
6. TCP connection closes its `io.Writer` signaling to the local app that the response is complete
7. local app sees the response is complete and sends one final message back to the codespace through the TCP connection's still-open reader which forwards to the ssh channel's still-open writer which forwards to the codespace's still-open reader
8. no reply can come from the codespace, so the local app closes its own writer
9. TCP connection reader reads EOF and exits the `io.Copy` call
10. ssh channel closes its `io.Writer` which terminates both the TCP connection and ssh channel

This PR specifically adds the logic in step 6. Without that new logic, step 8 can hang forever as the app may think the codespace might have data to send still.

The need to only half close the TCP connection is to support the scenario in step 7. If we fully closed the connection in step 6 then the local app couldn't send additional data to the codespace after getting the response.

> port forwarding tests have been disabled in CI due to being flakey

Thanks for the heads up! Ran locally and looks good

issue_context.title: `gh cs port forward` does not close http connection
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

> gh version 2.21.2 (2023-01-03)

I noticed a very weird behaviour when using the command `gh cs port forward 80:8888` to forward [PHP's Build-in Web Server](https://www.php.net/manual/en/features.commandline.webserver.php), the connection will not be closed.

![Screen recording of running a command "curl localhost:8888", which returns the output of phpinfo(), and the command stays running](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67255597/211847966-251cb6cc-c79c-4fbf-845a-ad954c7cda26.gif)
When using `curl`, it keeps running.

![A chromium browser window viewing at url localhost:8888, displaying the output of "phpinfo()". The spinner in front of the page title is spinning, indicates that the page is still loading. A debug window is opened, with the tab "network" shows a yellow warning text says "CAUTION: request is not finished yet!"](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67255597/211848924-97d78e07-0dd5-4ea8-86a0-d212843a7ca3.png)
The spinner on the page title of chromium browser keep spinning. "Network" developer tools show a warning says that the request is not finished.

What's even weird is that the response body is missing the last line.

This is what the output should look like, which is the output of the command `curl localhost:8888` inside the Codespaces instance:
![CleanShot 2023-01-12 at 00 00 49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67255597/211854900-e41b2985-def3-470c-bdb4-a76d7624da33.png)

Output on my local machine by running `curl localhost:8888`, where 8888 is forwarded by `gh` command:
![CleanShot 2023-01-12 at 00 01 17](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67255597/211855027-ad2bcdcb-218f-453b-81fa-aefcd9b6525c.png)

It only happens when forwarding ports using `gh cs port forward`, but not when using JetBrains IDE's port forwarding feature, nor when using `*.preview.app.github.dev` URL to access the port.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a new repository on GitHub. Then creates a file inside it to initialise a branch.
2. Create a new GitHub Codespace using the repository created in step 1.
3. Waiting for the Codespace to be created.
4. Open Terminal app on your local machine.
5. Run command `gh cs ssh` in the terminal window you just opened, then select the Codespace created in step 1.
6. Run command `echo "<?php phpinfo();" > info.php` inside the SSH connection to create a php file for test.
7. Run command `php -S 0.0.0.0:8888 info.php` to start PHP's build-in web server. Keep this terminal window opening.
8. Open a new terminal window on your local machine.
9. Run command `gh cs port forward 8888:8888` on the terminal window you opened in step 8. Keep this terminal window opening.
10. Open a new terminal window on your local machine.
11. Run command `curl localhost:8888`. The curl command will keep running until you hit `Ctrl-C` to terminate it.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected Behaviour: The command `curl localhost:8888` should stop after the http response received.
Actual Behaviour: The command `curl localhost:8888` does not stop even though the 

### Logs

Described in the steps to reproduce.

---- 

Update for anyone who are facing the same issue: You can use ssh tunnel as an alternative:
```
gh cs ssh -- -L 8703:localhost:80
```
will forward remote's `localhost:80` to the 8703 port on your local machine. If you need more than one port, just append more `-L` options:
```
gh cs ssh -- -L 8703:localhost:80 -L 5173:localhost:5173
```
comments:
I'm currently using SSH tunnel as an alternative.
I tried to read `cli`'s code, but unfortunately I don't have the ability to understand the part about port forwarding. It must be in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/ba27e5bfb88bab29021ae0eace03348e41f0b24f/pkg/liveshare/port_forwarder.go .  I don't have experience in Go lang thus don't know how to debug this code.

I don't have an explanation yet, but I spent a while digging into this and can repro the example. However, I do see that other simple apps do close the connection successfully - e.g. I tried a PHP server with `<?php echo('Hello, World') ?>` which worked as expected as well as a `python flask` hello world app.

@binotaliu I'm not very familiar with php - is it possible that `phpinfo` is doing something extra? Is it possible to boil the repro down to something where everything is explicit, rather than inside this function?

It does not only happen when using `phpinfo` but also happens when using [Laravel framework's build-in dev server](https://laravel.com/), which uses PHP's build-in web server underneath. So, even if the page does not uses `phpinfo`, it will still have this issue. 

I notice this issue when trying to setup a dev environment for Laravel development. Which involves a laravel's dev server, and a [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/) dev server. The Vite dev server's connections were properly closed. So I just assume the problem are somehow only exists in PHP. 

If a simple `echo "hello, world"` does not have this issue, is it possible related to content length?
I will try to find a more explicit repro.

Yeah, for some reason the basic `echo("Hello world")` working example stopped working for me also. Not sure what happened there, maybe some caching.

*(you can skip to the tl;dr if you don't care about implementation details)*

I dug into this more today and the hint about `Content-Length` does seem to be a good lead. I can repro the curl hang with this php:

```php
<?php
echo("Hello World");
?>
```

but this php does work:

```php
<?php
header("Content-Length: 11");
echo("Hello World");
?>
```

I dug into how the cli is handling the forwarding, and I think I understand why `Content-Length` is so important.

Port forwarding works by starting a `net.Conn` to accept the incoming request (curl in this case) as well has starting an `ssh.Channel` to tunnel into the codespace. These are set up to read from and write into each other using 2 `io.Copy` calls. The set up looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5447118/213535876-61b1036d-37a5-4f31-adf7-32d378c356c0.png)

The code blocks until both of the copies finish, meaning that both the `net.Conn` (from curl) and the `ssh.Channel` (from the codespace) read an EOF. I added logging to the cli and confirmed that the `ssh.Channel` does finish, but the `net.Conn` does not. That means that curl is holding the connection open - the reason for this is that since there is no `Content-Length`, curl does not know that the response is complete and so never closes.

# tl;dr

So the current solution is that the server code running in the codespace must ensure that it always returns a `Content-Length` header.

An alternative, which requires a code change in the cli, is that the cli can detect when the `ssh.Channel` has finished all writing and half-close the connection to curl using `TCPConn.CloseWrite`. I was able to do that fairly easily and show that that will indeed cause curl to also close its side of the connection.

Thanks for spending time on this! I can confirm that with the code in #6888 will correctly closes the connections.

The reason there is no `Content-Length` header is because PHP server won't wait for the whole script end before sending output back to user agent. Instead it sends output in a stream-ish way -- every time you `echo`-ed, the output will be send immediately back to user agent.

So if you request following script with curl:

```php
<?php

echo "hello, ";

sleep(10);

echo "world";
```

you will first see `hello, ` and then you wait 10 seconds to see `world`. The HTTP header must be send **before** body, so it is impossible for PHP to automatically calculate the value of `content-length`.
I believe it is also true when using other back-end languages like Python or Node.js, when http body are dynamically generated. Even `github.com` has no `content-length` header:

```bash
curl -I https://github.com
```

```http
HTTP/2 200 
server: GitHub.com
date: Sat, 21 Jan 2023 09:03:39 GMT
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
vary: X-PJAX, X-PJAX-Container, Turbo-Visit, Turbo-Frame, Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding, Accept, X-Requested-With
content-language: en-US
etag: W/"f829681b47ec944018028501c5c81b35"
cache-control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains; preload
x-frame-options: deny
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-xss-protection: 0
referrer-policy: origin-when-cross-origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin
content-security-policy: [...]
set-cookie: [...]
accept-ranges: bytes
x-github-request-id: [...]
```

review_comments: Just curious--can we reuse the `ListenTCP` method above instead of reimplementing it here? Am I maybe missing a cyclic dependency?
Yeah, it is a cyclic dependency between `codespaces` and `rpc` packages. The loop is `(rpc) invoker.go -> (codespaces) codespaces.go` and `(codespaces) states.go -> (rpc) invoker.go`
I'm considered making a whole third package just for `ListenTCP` but that felt like overkill :)
Open to suggestions for naming here 😅
Does the interface need to be public?

It doesn't technically need to be I don't think - the reason that I made it public is that it's exposed in the signature of `Forward` as well as `NewReadWriteHalfCloser` but nothing outside this file uses the name
